finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the POST parameter `feed` goes straight into file_get_contents(). The URL has no scheme, host or IP validation, so any client can make the server fetch http(s)://, ftp:// or other wrapper URLs. That reaches internal services, cloud metadata (169.254.169.254) and localhost. Local paths and file:// are also accepted. The response is not echoed, but its length is returned, which gives a blind oracle for whether a target is reachable and how large its response is.

trace.note: Handler is entered on any POST request that contains `feed`. There is no require_admin() call.
$_POST['feed'] is passed unchanged to file_get_contents(), which follows URL wrappers and HTTP redirects.
strlen($xml) is echoed back, leaking response size and reachability.

finding.guards_checked: There is no require_admin() call on this path, and no scheme or host allowlist. There is no private-IP or DNS check and no redirect restriction. Nothing was found that mitigates it. The admin-only webhook sink at line 20 is gated by require_admin(), so it is not reported.

verdict.reason: import.php:11-13 passes $_POST['feed'] unvalidated to file_get_contents() and echoes strlen($xml), with no require_admin() or host/scheme check on that path (require_admin() is only called at import.php:18 for the separate webhook handler).
